reason: Added two real, unmodified-code levers: team scoped per-key secrets-backend environment variables never reach the start-up log masker, and the synthetic per-key sensitivity rule is absent from the CLI list/get-value concealment paths.

levers.shape: team scoped per-key secrets-backend environment variables (AIRFLOW__<TEAM>___SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARG__<KEY> and the workers spelling) stay unregistered with the start-up secrets masker
levers.skip_reason: different output channel (start-up/worker log redaction) reached through a producer that enumerates only the deployment-wide env prefix; the published fix itself documents the secrets backend as not team aware, and the API already hides the same values
levers.coupled: deployment-wide per-key env values remain redacted; a non-sensitive team env value is not redacted
levers.fairness: No team-scoped override of an option whose deployment-wide counterpart Airflow conceals as sensitive may be disclosed in clear text anywhere Airflow conceals sensitive configuration or removes sensitive values from the output it produces, however the override is supplied

levers.shape: team scoped per-key secrets-backend entries in the CLI config listing and get-value hide paths (secrets and workers, including a team name containing the separator), which must keep the exact `< hidden >` form and still succeed
levers.skip_reason: the per-key rule lives in the API service module, outside the registered option list; a solver who fixes the API per-key masking stops there, and the local admin CLI looks out of scope because deployment-wide per-key values are visible there today
levers.coupled: deployment-wide per-key values and non-sensitive team values stay readable in the same output; display_sensitive=True still returns real values
levers.fairness: No team-scoped override ... may be disclosed ... at every interface and every granularity at which configuration is presented, however the override is supplied

fail_confidence_reason: Two new independent real-code traps each need a separate mechanism to be understood (the per-key env collector behind log registration, and the per-key classification rule inside the CLI write/get-value paths), while the pre-existing arbitrary-team-name and log-registration traps were already missed once by the solving model; a thorough solver that follows the per-key rule across channels could still cover both, so 0/3 for both models is plausible but not certain.
